title: Newspaper Clipping - Municipal Salaries

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
C. & S. C. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 3122.
31.

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, JANUARY 22, 1932

MUNICIPAL SALARIES
“Trifling” Economies

To the Editor of the
“NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.”

SIR,—I am not nor ever have been an employee of the S.M.C. so I write without prejudice or any bias when I attempt a counterblast against those who enter your columns with suggestions of economy on the lines of reductions of salary or restricting home leave to periods with “a minimum of 10 to 15 years service.”

I am afraid that such correspondents must be of that mean employers class which does not like the example of decent wage and leave provision set by Shanghai’s biggest employing body the S.M.C.

Reductions in salary are nothing but income tax in effect if not in name and if inevitable should like income tax have a level of exemption and be in every way similar to this tax in England as regards relief for the family man and be graduated to bring the weight on to the shoulders of those able to bear it. As to home leave I have worked under contract for a Shanghai firm and salaried home leave with passage paid both ways was an integral part of my contract. I take it that the S.M.C. employees are protected by similar contract provisions and therefore no effect would be seen in tax reduction until the present contracts expire by which time we hope that better times will have arrived.

Another point which seems always to be neglected by public advocates of this kind of economy is to find out and tell us how much reduction of rates will ensue from their schemes. Let us take the concrete case above and put it in this form: If leave is restricted to once in 15 years the rates will be reduced by X. How much is X? Perhaps some statistician having access to the Council’s books will give us the result.

To me it seems as though too many people are willing to sacrifice hundreds of dollars of other people’s incomes in order to save trifling sums per annum on their own.

ARTHUR LEEVE.
Shanghai, Jan. 19, 1932.

（批：Read by S.A.）

《字林西报》，1932年1月22日，星期五

市政薪金
“微不足道”的节约

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生，——我过去不是、现在也不是工部局的雇员，因此当我试图对那些在贵报专栏中建议通过减薪或将休假限制为“至少服务10至15年”方可享受等措施来实行节约的人士进行反驳时，我是毫无成见或偏颇的。

恐怕这类通信者属于那种吝啬的雇主阶层，他们不喜欢上海最大的雇佣机构工部局所树立的关于体面工资和休假规定的榜样。

减薪实质上就是所得税，即便名义上不是如此；如果减薪不可避免，那么它应当像所得税一样设有免税额度，并且在各方面都类似于英国的这种税收，即对有家庭负担者给予减免，并采用累进制，将重担压在那些有能力承担的人肩上。至于回国休假，我曾根据合同为上海一家商行工作，带薪回国休假且双向船票由雇主支付是我合同的一个组成部分。我想工部局雇员也受到类似合同条款的保护，因此在现有合同到期之前，税收方面不会看到任何效果，而到那时，我们希望更好的时机已经到来。

提倡此类节约措施的公众人士似乎总是忽视另一点，即查明并告诉我们，他们的方案会导致捐税减少多少。让我们以上述具体案例为例，将其表述如下：如果将休假限制为每15年一次，捐税将减少X。X是多少？也许某些能够查阅工部局账簿的统计学家能给我们提供结果。

在我看来，似乎有太多的人愿意牺牲他人数百美元的收入，以便为自己每年节省微不足道的金额。

亚瑟·利夫 (Arthur Leeve)
上海，1932年1月19日。

（批注：S.A. 阅）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. P. D. 5122.
21. 1. 32.

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 20, 1932

MUNICIPAL FINANCE
Passages for Officials
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS."

SIR,—With regard to the letter
from "J. C." in this morning's issue
of your paper, most rate-payers will
agree, I think, that economy could
be effected with regard to home
leave of municipal employees. Is
there any reason, for instance, why
such a large number are allowed
first-class fares, whereas many
rate-payers have to travel second,
and are content to do so? A few
years ago a Municipal Council em-
ployee with his family returned
from long leave. He had been back
only about a year when it was time
for him to retire. They went home
again, first class fares provided.
Another employee with his family
returned about fourteen months ago.
He retires in a few months time,
and goes home again on first class
fares. These are two known cases
to the writer, but doubtless there
are others. One does not blame the
individuals concerned, for many
would appreciate being in the same
boat, but cases of this kind do not
exactly spell economy. Increases in
municipal rates and school fees will
without doubt cause a good deal of
hardship to many rate-payers at the
present difficult time.

FAIR PLAY.
Shanghai, Jan. 19, 1932.

[Editor's Note.—In accordance with the practice
prevailing in most Governments, first
class passages are granted to employees of
a certain rank and above; those of lower
class, etc., go second class.]

（批：Reg.
Please keep.
gph
20/1/32）

《字林西报》，1932年1月20日，星期三

市政财政
官员的船票

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生，——关于贵报今晨刊登的“J. C.”的来信，我想大多数纳税人都会同意，在市政雇员的回国休假问题上是可以实现节约的。例如，有什么理由允许如此众多的人员享受头等舱船票，而许多纳税人不得不乘坐二等舱，并且对此感到满意呢？几年前，一名工部局雇员携家人从长期休假归来。他回来仅约一年，就到了退休的时候。他们再次回国，提供了头等舱船票。另一名雇员携家人于约十四个月前归来。他将在几个月后退休，并再次乘坐头等舱回国。这是笔者所知的两个案例，但无疑还有其他案例。人们并不责怪相关个人，因为许多人会羡慕处于同样的境地，但这类案例确实算不上节约。在目前困难时期，市政捐税和学校费用的增加无疑会给许多纳税人造成相当大的困难。

公平对待 (Fair Play)
上海，1932年1月19日。

[编者按：——按照大多数政府通行的做法，一定职级及以上的雇员授予头等舱船票；较低职级等人员则乘坐二等舱。]

（批注：登记。
请存档。
gph
1932年1月20日）

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, JANUARY 19, 1932

MUNICIPAL ECONOMY
The Holiday Question
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS."
SIR,—After perusing page 46 of
to-day's Municipal Gazette on the
Council's deliberations on the Fin-
ancial Situation for 1932, one feels
impelled to turn back to page 45
and enquire whether an economy
cannot be effected in the matter of
Long Leaves.
We find:
2 Chief Inspectors
9 British and Russian Sergeants
2 Assistant Nurses
and 4 Assistant School Mistresses
due for Long Leave within the next
4 or 5 months.
The pertinent question is how
many of those who have to foot the
bill (14 per cent. at present with
bright prospects of a raised 2 per
cent. soon) ever themselves have
a chance of getting such extensive
leaves?
Should not a minimum of, say,
10 or 15 years of service be re-
quired before such Leaves be con-
sidered?
Shanghai is not such an unhealthy
place that one must needs run away
every 4 or 5 years for 4 or 5 months
to try and forget the terrible
climate.
W. C.
Shanghai, Jan. 18, 1932.

（批：Reg. Please keep. W.S. 19/1/32）

《字林西报》，1932年1月19日，星期二

市政节约
休假问题

致《字林西报》编辑：
先生，——在细读了今日《市政公报》第46页关于工部局对1932年财政状况的审议内容后，人们不禁想翻回第45页，询问在长期休假问题上是否不能实行节约。
我们发现：
2名总巡长
9名英籍和俄籍巡长
2名助理护士
以及4名助理女教师
将在未来4或5个月内享有长期休假。
 pertinent 问题是，那些必须买单的人（目前为14%，很快有望提高2%）中，有多少人自己有机会获得如此长时间的休假？
在考虑此类休假之前，是否应要求至少服务，比如说，10或15年？
上海并不是一个如此不健康的地方，以至于人们必须每4或5年就逃离4或5个月，以试图忘记那可怕的气候。

W. C.
上海，1932年1月18日。

（批注：登记。请存档。W.S. 1932年1月19日）
